key_insight: The paper gives optimal stochastic algorithms for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization with convex constraints, matching lower bounds for finding a (δ, ε)-Goldstein stationary point.
engineering_relevance: This provides theoretically optimal solver rates for constrained machine-learning and control problems where objectives are noisy, nonsmooth, and nonconvex.
method: Projection-based stochastic gradient method with \u007eO(δ^{-1}ε^{-3}) complexity
Projection-free / Frank-Wolfe-style variant with the same optimal rate
Zeroth-order extension with \u007eO(dδ^{-1}ε^{-3}) complexity, optimal in dimension dependence
evidence_signal: The abstract reports matching upper and lower complexity bounds, including a lower bound stated via the Frank-Wolfe gap and valid even for smooth problems.
watch_item: The optimal rates are asymptotic and rely on convex constraints plus stochastic oracle assumptions, so practical performance may still depend strongly on projection cost, noise level, and tuning.
paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization with Constraints
